On due consideration, I.A. No.15152/2019 is allowed and delay of 119 days in filing this appeal is hereby condoned.

5. These miscellaneous appeals under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 are filed by the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. and the claimants, respectively, being aggrieved of award dated 04.05.2019 passed by the learned Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal (M.P.)
in MACC No.550/2017 (Smt.Sudha Pachori and others Vs. Yasir Muztaba and others).

sentences.text: 6. Shri Vineet Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the insurance company submits that FIR was lodged against an unknown car but later on, scooter driven by non-applicant No.1 Yasir Muztaba and owned by non-applicant No.2 Parvez Anzum has been falsely implicated as it was insured with the appellant- Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.

Reading from the FIR, it is submitted that this aspect has been overlooked and thus, it is a clear case of false implication of the offending vehicle so to extract undue compensation from the insurer.
7.

Shri Nitin Gupta, learned counsel for the claimants submits that claimants have filed appeal for enhancement of compensation on the ground that age of the deceased was 50 years and 2 months,
therefore, looking to the age of the deceased, multiplier of 13 should have been applied, whereas Tribunal has wrongly applied multiplier of 11 and also wrongly applied Future Prospects at 10%,
whereas it should have been 30%.
8.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, there is an important aspect to this case.
Investigating Officer was examined before the learned Claims Tribunal.
His evidence was adduced before the Tribunal.
Investigating Officer Shri Sarvesh Singh S/o Surendra Bahadur Singh, ASI, Police Station M.P. Nagar was cross-
examined by learned counsel for the respondent No.3-Oriental Insurance Company, namely, Shri R.S. Parihar.

He did not give any suggestion to the Investigating Officer that how come when FIR was lodged against unknown car,
final report was submitted against a two wheeler.
This reflects glaring lapse on the part of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

Shri Vineet Pandey could not overcome this lapse on the part of their own counsel while cross-examining the Investigating Officer though the main ground taken by the insurance company is that FIR was lodged against a car and scooter has been implicated.
This reflects the lapse on the part of the insurance company and their counsel in not properly cross-examining the Investigating Officer.

sentences.text: This appeal appears to be frivolously filed.

When a ground so vehemently raised by the insurance company in their appeal, is not taken while cross-examining the Investigating officer, author of the FIR and final report on the basis of which award has been passed then this Court has no hesitation to hold that this is a frivolous appeal filed without any basis.
Therefore, appeal filed by the insurance company deserves to be and is hereby dismissed.
10. As far as appeal (M.A. No.1678/2020) filed by the claimants is concerned, age of the deceased was 50 years, 2 months.
His date of birth has come on record as 30.06.1966.
Date of the accident is 20.08.2016.
He had not completed 51 years of age, therefore, multiplier of 13 will be applicable and not that of 11.

Similarly, there is a certificate issued by Dainik Bhaskar Group as contained in Ex.P-7 in which it is mentioned that Shri Karan Prasad Pachori was working with Dainik Bhaskar Group as Record Keeper Grade S1, Employee Code 11830 since 01 st August, 2004 and salary slip for May,
2016 is enclosed as Ex.P-5 was issued by the said Dainik Bhaskar Group.
Similarly, salary slip for June, 2016 is also enclosed as Ex.P-8.
Thus, there is no iota of doubt that the deceased was a salaried employee.

Therefore, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, (2017) 16 SCC 680 Future Prospect is to be computed at the rate of 30% in place of 10% as has been computed by the learned Claims Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. Thus, when these aspects are taken into consideration, Tribunal has accepted income of the deceased at Rs.7,967/- per month or Rs,95,604/- per annum.
As deceased is survived by four legal heirs, therefore, when 1/4 th deduction is made towards living expenses of the deceased, net dependency will come out to Rs.71,703/- per annum.

30% is added towards the Future Prospects,
taking total compensation to Rs.93,214/-.

Multiplier of 13 will be applicable, taking total pecuniary compensation to Rs.12,11,782/-, over and above which claimants will be entitled to a sum of Rs.70,000/- under the head of non-pecuniary compensation, besides this

Claimants No.2 to 4 are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each in the light of the law laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in United India Insurance Company Limited versus Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kour 2020 SCC Online SC 410 for loss of parental consortium, taking total compensation to Rs.14,01,782/-
against a sum of Rs.10,42,504/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited versus Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kour 2020 SCC Online SC 410
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.3,59,278/- (Rupees Three Lakhs, Fifty Nine Thousands, two Hundred and seventy eight only) to which claimants will be entitled to in addition to the amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
This additional amount will also earn interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
13. This additional amount along with accrued interest shall remain invested in the Monthly Income Scheme of the Indian Post Office or a Nationalized Bank for a period of five years.
The claimants will be entitled to utilize its monthly interest for their well being and maintenance, but the principal amount will not allowed to be withdrawn for a period of five years.
14. In above terms, these miscellaneous appeals are disposed of.
15. Record of the Claims Tribunal be sent back.

11. Thus, when these aspects are taken into consideration, Tribunal has accepted income of the deceased at Rs.7,967/- per month or Rs,95,604/- per annum.
